subject: NorthBridge deployment: connection selection for private deployment
messages:
From: Peter Hall <phall@northbridge.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@northbridge.com
Date: 2028-07-22T16:12:00Z
Subject: NorthBridge: private inference deployment — connectivity options

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to move toward a private deployment for our inference workload. Before we schedule an on-site network walkthrough, NetOps asked for a recommendation on the connectivity model: VPC peering, PrivateLink/interface endpoints, or a site-to-site VPN (IPSec).

Key constraints:
- Sensitive PII in requests, so we prefer minimizing egress over public internet.
- Target latency: <40ms p95 from our app nodes to inference endpoints.
- Budget: we have an initial 12-month cap for network transit/storage costs; we can expand if savings are clear.

Can Redwood outline the tradeoffs and call out any blockers for a pilot (e.g., cross-account routing limits, transitive peering, IP overlap)? I've attached our high-level infra diagram.

(attachment: northbridge_infra_overview.pdf)

Thanks,
Peter Hall
Head of Platform Engineering — NorthBridge Financial
phall@northbridge.com
From: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-22T17:34:00Z
Subject: Re: NorthBridge: private inference deployment — connectivity options

Peter — thanks for the clear constraints and the diagram. High level summary up front: for your requirements we usually recommend PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for shortest control-plane and data-plane isolation, with a VPN fallback for quick pilots. VPC peering works where both VPCs can accept routable IP ranges with no overlap, but it becomes operationally brittle at scale (transitive limitations, route table sprawl).

Quick asks from our side to finalize a recommendation:
- Confirm whether NorthBridge will accept AWS Interface Endpoints (if on AWS) or whether you need an on-prem-only link.
- Any existing transitive peering/hub-and-spoke that would prevent direct peering?
- Preferred CIDR ranges (we need to run overlap checks).

I'll loop in Olga (network architect) and Kimberly (private deploy lead) to provide a short tradeoffs memo and a diagram of the recommended pilot topology.

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: phall@northbridge.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-22T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: NorthBridge: private inference deployment — connectivity options

Markus / team / Peter — I ran a quick comparison based on NorthBridge constraints. Summary (concise):

1) PrivateLink (interface endpoint)
- Pros:
  - Strong data-plane isolation; traffic stays inside cloud fabric (no public IP NAT for each request).
  - Per-endpoint IAM + security groups; easier to audit and restrict access by service principals.
  - Predictable latency, minimal NAT traversal overhead.
- Cons:
  - Additional per-GB data processing charges from cloud provider + endpoint-hour costs.
  - Requires endpoint configuration in each customer VPC/subnet; adds setup time for multi-AZ.
  - If NorthBridge uses on-prem only (no cloud VPC), this is not applicable without a cloud transit.

2) VPC Peering
- Pros:
  - Simple L3 routing between VPCs when CIDRs are non-overlapping.
  - No endpoint-hour costs; charges limited to inter-AZ/inter-region data costs.
- Cons:
  - Not transitive (complex with hub-and-spoke).
  - CIDR overlap is a hard blocker; difficult for large enterprises with many networks.
  - Harder to apply fine-grained access controls per-service.

3) Site-to-Site VPN (IPSec)
- Pros: quick to stand up for pilots; supports on-prem only scenarios; encrypted over public internet if private links not yet authorized.
- Cons:
  - Potentially higher and unpredictable latency/jitter; depends on internet path.
  - Throughput limits on common VPN gateways; need to size and test.
  - Ongoing operational overhead for keys, rotations, uptime SLAs.

Recommendation for NorthBridge pilot:
- If you can host a VPC in the same cloud region as Redwood private deployment, start with PrivateLink for production-facing MLPs and use a short-term VPN for the initial connectivity validation.
- If on-prem only and you need to avoid cloud-hosted VPCs, propose a dedicated S2S VPN with a monitored throughput baseline; plan to upgrade to a Direct Connect / Cloud Interconnect + PrivateLink pattern for production.

Next steps I can own:
- Overlap check (please share CIDRs)
- Pilot topology diagram showing PrivateLink + fallthrough VPN (I attached a draft)
- Cost estimate (I started a workbook)

(attachment: connectivity_cost_model.xlsx)

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Network Architect — Redwood Inference
From: Peter Hall <phall@northbridge.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-22T22:48:00Z
Subject: Re: NorthBridge: private inference deployment — connectivity options

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear tradeoffs.

Decision: we will proceed with a two-stage approach:
1) Pilot: stand up a lab VPC in our AWS account and connect via VPN to validate latency and throughput, run a small inference workload for 72 hours.
2) Production: if pilot meets latency and stability targets, move to PrivateLink (interface endpoint) in our production VPC and decommission the VPN for steady-state.

Action items assigned to Redwood:
- Olga: run CIDR overlap check and send recommended endpoint subnets + diagram (due: 2028-07-25)
- Kimberly: provide a short runbook for creating interface endpoints in multi-AZ (due: 2028-07-24)
- Markus: coordinate a 90-min pilot kickoff call next week and share invites

I'll start internal procurement for the lab VPC and will share the account IDs once approved. Please add any risks I missed.

Thanks,
Peter Hall
Head of Platform Engineering — NorthBridge Financial
